segments.text: If we should graunt this doctrine to be true, then must we needes allow of these absurdities in diuinitie, which follow. I. That God would haue all, and each singular man to be saued: and withall he would haue some ordained to hatred, and perdition: or, That in regard of God, all men are elected, and redeemed, but in regard of the euent many perish. II. The guilt of Adams sinne must not be imputed to any one of his posteritie, because that God, hauing mercie of all generally in Christ, did take into the couenant of reconciliatiō all mankind. Now if but the guiltines of Adams fall be taken away, the punishment forthwith ceaseth to be a punishment, and corruption it selfe is by little and little abolished in all men.
